note: Every cell below is grounded in a numbered design-freeze finding. Cells whose CONSTRUCTION has not been proven possible are marked constructibility NOT_PROVEN and are an input to V2-R9-FIXTURE, not a licence to run them.
global_preconditions: X launched with -noreset (D-01). Without it, the last X client disconnecting silently and permanently kills Gate A (Q10), and every 'Gate A inactive' observation becomes unattributable.
Product dc94485 or later: D-02's epoch records and finalization latch are required for any multi-epoch observation to be recorded at all (Q4-F3).
Every boundary records the full field set from r9-identity-contract.json required_evidence_fields.per_boundary.

cells.name: warm rebind, drained tables
cells.construction: X1 completes a clean GENERATION_CLOSE so the renderer unbinds (renderer.cpp:813) and the Gate A tables drain. X1 exits. The Activity survives on the HUP_UNBOUND arm. A new X2 connects to the same Activity.
must_prove: activity_process UNCHANGED across the boundary
x_process CHANGED
generation advanced by exactly 1; epoch_id advanced by exactly 1
R_EPOCH_BEGIN for epoch 2 carries the NEW tuple and epoch_id=2
the EGL context and GL objects were RETAINED, not rebuilt (Q4/F2: ctx is never destroyed and refreshContext swaps only the surface)
forbidden: proving WARM from the launch method (§8.4)
asserting a renderer END for epoch 1 — the END is now whole-run, not per-epoch (D-02)
cells.constructibility: PLAUSIBLE. Depends on the Activity actually taking the HUP_UNBOUND arm after a clean close. Q11 proved a BOUND Activity always dies with X, and the clean close is what unbinds it, so the ordering is the whole question. NOT PROVEN.
cells.disposition_basis: ASTRA 2026-09-22, option (c). No product entry point for a same-Activity warm reconnect: all three tryConnect() call sites are blocked (singleInstance blocks onCreate re-entry; onReceiveConnection needs a Binder the shell cannot marshal; the third is gated on !connected, and connected() is literally conn_fd != -1). Testing a path the product cannot reach would require a second X display (breaking the :3-only boundary) or an artificial test seam.

cells.name: warm rebind over LIVE imports — containment halt
cells.construction: Cause the Activity to call connect_ with a new fd WITHOUT the old X dying, while the renderer still holds a READY import. connect_ (activity.cpp:544-550) resets the socket, the mapping and the legacy buffer lists but NOT gateABound and NOT the Gate A tables, so the next gateABindFromState meets a still-bound Activity with live imports.
must_prove: lorieGateAFatalHalt("r-rebind-busy", FAIL_GENERATION) fired
the stale READY was NOT consumed by the new generation
the halt is the EXPECTED outcome, not a failure
forbidden: writing this as a success path — Q1-F1 makes it a HALT packet
accepting absence of consumption as the proof; the halt must be positively observed
cells.constructibility: NOT_PROVEN, and this is the hardest cell in the set. It requires a Java-driven reconnect (MainActivity.tryConnect -> service.getXConnection -> LorieView.connect) while the previous X is still alive and bound. The runner currently has no mechanism to trigger that. V2-R9-FIXTURE must either find one or declare this cell INVALID_CONSTRUCTION.
cells.disposition_basis: ASTRA 2026-09-22, option (c). Same entry-point absence. The r-rebind-busy containment is already source-proven by Q1-F1 and Q5 with four independent filters; adding a test-only entry point to observe the fatal once more is not worth a product cycle.

cells.name: warm reconnect with no state fd — Q4-F1 regression
cells.construction: Drive a warm reconnect (connect_ with a new fd), then let the new X die BEFORE it sends EVENT_SHARED_SERVER_STATE. Pre-dc94485 this dereferenced a munmap'd gateAMappedState in the peer-HUP handler.
must_prove: no SIGSEGV and no unclassified crash
the peer-HUP classified normally (HUP_R_HUP with published==0, since gateAMappedState is now NULL)
gateAMappedState was cleared, i.e. the dc94485 fix is live
forbidden: running this against any product earlier than dc94485
cells.constructibility: NOT_PROVEN. Requires winning a race against the 250 ms MainActivity retry loop (Q1-F2). May be unreachable deliberately; if so, record that the fix is unfalsifiable at runtime and rely on the source proof instead.
cells.disposition_basis: ASTRA 2026-09-22, option (c). Same entry-point absence. The Q4-F1 fix is source-verified and pinned by five static checks in verify-r8-support.py.

cells.name: cold Activity restart, terminal old registry
cells.construction: X survives. The Activity process is killed and restarted. Its old generation's X-side registry is TERMINAL (no pendingCount, no lastSubmittedSerial). The next lorieActivityConnected() bumps the generation.
must_prove: activity_process CHANGED (pid OR starttime differs) — the ONLY valid COLD discriminator (Q2-F2)
epoch_id RESET to 1 on the new renderer process
sessionNonce UNCHANGED (it is per X process, Q3), generation advanced by 1
the Activity-side world was genuinely rebuilt: a NEW EGL context, new stateCondFd (Q2, renderer.cpp:1229-1232 'if (ctx) return' did not trip)
X-side survivors are unchanged: gpuCopySerialCounter continued monotonically, registeredBuffers, the shared region
forbidden: using the notification-bar Exit as proof of process death (V-8)
using (nonce, generation) to classify this as COLD (Q2-F2)
cells.constructibility: PLAUSIBLE. Killing the Activity process is directly drivable. The condition to arrange is that the old registry is terminal.
cells.disposition_basis: COLD1-ROUTE-SEARCH.md: no drivable published renderer fatal exists with a TERMINAL registry. All 26 gateARendererFatal sites enumerated; the only pre-lease test-fault site (674) does not fatal the renderer, and every published fatal is strictly between lease and ack.

cells.name: cold restart with NON-terminal old registry — containment halt
cells.construction: Same as COLD-1 but leave an old-generation registry entry with pendingCount != 0 or lastSubmittedSerial != 0 at the moment of the bump.
must_prove: lorieGateAFatalHalt("x-bump-unterminal", FAIL_GENERATION) fired from cmdentrypoint.cpp:389-393
the new generation was NOT opened
forbidden: treating the halt as a failure — it is the designed containment
cells.constructibility: NOT_PROVEN. Requires holding a registry entry non-terminal across an Activity death, which Q11 suggests is hard: a bound Activity dies with X, and the paths that leave work non-terminal tend to be fatal paths that kill X too.
cells.disposition_basis: CONSTRUCTIBLE via fault 8 (RENDERER_FATAL_PRE_FENCE): publishes fatal so X survives, and fires strictly between the lease (cmdentrypoint.cpp:226-227) and the ack (:270-271) so pendingCount stays 1, which is exactly what x-bump-unterminal detects.

cells.name: cold restart, dual-authority identity recording
cells.construction: A COLD restart whose sole purpose is to record BOTH tuple authorities and both process identities at the boundary, proving the evidence schema itself works.
must_prove: shared (nonce, generation) AND renderer-latched (nonce, generation) both recorded at the boundary
both process identities recorded as (PID, starttime)
epoch_id present and independent of generation
x_fd_table_had_previous_conn_fd recorded from /proc (Q9-F1 — the product reports nothing here)
forbidden: omitting any field in r9-identity-contract.json required_evidence_fields
cells.constructibility: PLAUSIBLE — it is COLD-1 plus a stricter evidence schema.
cells.disposition_basis: Inherits COLD-1: it is COLD-1 plus a stricter evidence schema.

cells.name: stale-ready replay — expected containment fatal
cells.construction: Per V-11 the frozen direction is enum16 / side2 -> x-wrong-generation / reason 6. Genuinely deliver an old-generation READY or frame into the current path.
must_prove: the EXACT expected fatal fired (x-wrong-generation, reason 6)
the stale state was not accepted and current-generation state was not polluted
forbidden: concluding PASS from 'nothing bad happened' — §8.8 requires the exact expected fatal
designing this as a defence. Q5 proved a stale READY is NOT reachable by a new generation (four independent filters), and Q6 proved the frame path is fatal on mismatch. F1's job is to PROVE THE HALT.
cells.constructibility: NOT_PROVEN, and Q5/Q6 make it harder than V-11 assumed. Every route to deliver stale state is already filtered or fatal. V2-R9-FIXTURE must show a construction that actually reaches the current path, or F1 is INVALID_CONSTRUCTION — which per §8.8 is NOT the same as VALID_FAIL.
cells.disposition_basis: CONSTRUCTIBLE via fault 16 (STALE_READY_REPLAY, renderer.cpp:674-679), which is built into the product. All four V-11 components verified: enum16 / side2 / x-wrong-generation / FAIL_GENERATION = 6.

cells.name: fresh session recovery after F1's fatal
cells.construction: Only after F1 has produced its expected fatal. Start a fresh session and drive a clean Gate A direct composite.
must_prove: NEW nonce (structural: the region is anonymous and a fresh X process memsets it and re-draws getrandom — Q11 (a))
EMPTY registry on both sides (structural for a new process pair — Q11 (b))
a clean direct exact SUCCESS, i.e. event=5 LEASE_GPU_OWNED present in the ring
the Activity process ACTUALLY DIED across the boundary — recorded as (PID, starttime), not inferred from socket closure (Q11-F1)
forbidden: manufacturing another fatal to satisfy the precondition — §8.8: if F1's expected fatal does not exist, F2 is BLOCKED
judging residue against an unwindowed logcat capture (Q11-F2: the obs sink survives process death and logcat -c is a redline; use the -T window and record logcat-since.txt)
cells.constructibility: PLAUSIBLE once F1 exists. Q11 found no source-level obstacle.
cells.disposition_basis: CONSTRUCTIBLE once F1's expected fatal exists. Q11 found no source-level obstacle.

cells_removed_from_the_plan.disposition: DOES NOT EXIST. Q10 found that a same-process reset path ALREADY exists (X server DE_RESET, the default), that it runs the Gate A clean close, and that it leaves Gate A PERMANENTLY DISABLED because the nonce allocator is guarded off after its single run. The packet is constructible but its only honest verdict is 'Gate A is dead afterwards' — it cannot demonstrate recovery, which is what the plan wanted from it. D-01 accepted -noreset and deferred same-process DE_RESET out of V1-Core scope.
cells_removed_from_the_plan.replaced_by: Nothing in R9. If a genuine reset is ever wanted, Q10 Part 5 enumerates the seven changes it would require.

cells_removed_from_the_plan.why: x-bump-unterminal (cmdentrypoint.cpp:391) requires a SECOND lorieActivityConnected() with generation != 0. X outlives its Activity only when lorieGateAActive() is already false (InitOutput.c:620-624); the clean close zeroes sessionNonce as well as generation (InitOutput.c:3334-3335) so the bump is gated off forever (InitOutput.c:567); and every fatal publisher that would clear the gate exits the X process in the same breath - X-side via lorieGateAFatalHalt _exit(127) (lorie.h:1414-1416), renderer-side because all 14 publish sites fire while X is inside gateAWaitTerminal for that serial (InitOutput.c:3539 -> lorie.h:296-297 -> InitOutput.c:3546 -> :3212-3217).
cells_removed_from_the_plan.retracts: COLD1-ROUTE-SEARCH.md preamble: condition 3 was 'X does NOT take the x-eof fatal'; it must read 'X is still running when the next Activity connects', which no published renderer fatal satisfies.
cells_removed_from_the_plan.reopen_if: the product gains a renderer fatal publisher reachable OUTSIDE an X terminal wait, OR a warm reconnect/rebind entry point (the same one that would reopen WARM-1/2/3).

plan_corrections_forced_by_the_freeze.target: §8.7 common proof list, item 'no stale READY 被新 generation 消費'
plan_corrections_forced_by_the_freeze.correction: Q5 proved this is structurally impossible (four independent filters). Proving ABSENCE of consumption is therefore a tautology. The provable obligation is that the designed HALT fired. Restate as 'the expected containment halt fired'.

plan_corrections_forced_by_the_freeze.target: §8.7 WARM-1/2/3 as a uniform success chain
plan_corrections_forced_by_the_freeze.correction: Q1-F1 makes warm-rebind-over-live-imports a HALT, not a success. The three WARM packets must be differentiated by table state, not merely numbered.
Add the Activity process identity as the REQUIRED discriminator. Q2-F2 proved (nonce, generation) cannot distinguish the two cases.
No longer conditional — they are DONE. D-02 required product support; dc94485 is built, installed and smoke-passed (R8-D, R8-P2).

disposition_note: SOURCE_PROVEN_RUNTIME_NOT_CONSTRUCTIBLE is NOT PASS, NOT FAIL, NOT INVALID and NOT runtime-qualified. Each such cell names the condition that would reopen it. If the product later gains a warm reconnect entry point, or a published renderer fatal at a pre-lease point, the affected cells MUST be reopened.
product_level_finding: GATE A HAS NO REACHABLE GENERATION BOUNDARY AT ALL. Superseding the earlier 'no reachable CLEAN same-process boundary': the bump path (InitOutput.c:565-589) runs exactly once per X process, on the first lorieActivityConnected(), which takes the generation == 0 branch and sets generation 1. A second one is unreachable (COLD2-ROUTE-SEARCH.md §C-§E). Consequently lorieGateARegistryCloseGeneration (cmdentrypoint.cpp:380) has no runtime caller, and x-bump-unterminal (cmdentrypoint.cpp:391) and x-share-in-lease (InitOutput.c:570) are defensive-only. Corroboration, not proof: across every Gate A run recorded under evidence/ (201989 GATEA_EVENT lines) generation has never been observed above 1. Belongs to D-06; recorded, not decided.
